Board of Governors AAS: eligibility and residency review

Review this associate-completion route only if you meet current Board of Governors entry rules. It may provide a useful credential or a specific bachelor’s-entry bridge, but older no-residency recipes are obsolete leads.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Associate completion
  • Prior-learning evaluation
  • Conditional credential bridge

What needs to be confirmed

  • Current age, prior-learning, graded-credit and residency rules need official confirmation.
  • Research records conflicting twelve- versus fifteen-credit residency reports after 2024.
  • A bridge must improve the complete bachelor’s route after added work, charges and conferral delay.
  • Required institutional courses and delivery format remain to be confirmed.
  • No current Pierpont numeric cap, residency requirement or price is verified in this catalog. Conflicting community numbers are not used as rules.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Get current Board of Governors eligibility before treating this as available.
  • A later BAS may require a specific associate type and technical-credit content; this award alone does not establish eligibility.

A practical sequence

  1. Confirm current eligibility, award and delivery format.
  2. Get official residency, graded-credit rules and prior-credit evaluation.
  3. Assemble GE/elective requirements from actual accepted awards.
  4. Compare direct bachelor’s entry with the entire bridge sequence.
  5. Finish required Pierpont work and submit all records.
  6. Obtain conferral before using the associate for a later admission gate.

Your next useful actions

  • Ask Pierpont to resolve current residency and full charges in writing.
  • Check whether the associate is needed for the intended next degree.
  • Compare the bridge with direct bachelor’s entry.

Official & supporting sources

  • Pierpont route and changed residency evidenceChecked 2026-10-30
  • UMPI YourPace FAQ: transfer and residencyChecked 2026-10-31
Ask for an individual evaluation.

Credit limits, degree placement, institutional-credit requirements, and professional eligibility are separate decisions. Use the current catalog and get the receiving school’s written confirmation.
